content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. In confessióne beátæ Margarítæ.
content.english: Ant. Let us praise our God.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Laudémus Deum nostrum * In confessióne beátæ Margarítæ.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. In confessióne beátæ Margarítæ.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

content.latin: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adiútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
content.english: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

content.latin: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
content.english: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

content.latin: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine eius.
content.english: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

content.latin: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
content.english: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

content.latin: 45:6 Deus in médio eius, non commovébitur: * adiuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
content.english: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

content.latin: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
content.english: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

content.latin: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Iacob.
content.english: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

content.latin: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
content.english: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

content.latin: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
content.english: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

content.latin: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
content.english: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

content.latin: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis in civitáte Dei nostri, ‡ in monte sancto eius.
content.english: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God, ‡ in his holy mountain.

content.latin: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
content.english: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

content.latin: 47:4 Deus in dómibus eius cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
content.english: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

content.latin: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
content.english: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

content.latin: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
content.english: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

content.latin: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
content.english: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

content.latin: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
content.english: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

content.latin: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
content.english: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

content.latin: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * iustítia plena est déxtera tua.
content.english: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

content.latin: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Iudæ: * propter iudícia tua, Dómine.
content.english: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

content.latin: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus eius.
content.english: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

content.latin: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte eius: * et distribúite domos eius, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
content.english: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

content.latin: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
content.english: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

content.latin: 48:2 Audíte hæc, omnes gentes: * áuribus percípite omnes, qui habitátis orbem:
content.english: 48:2 Hear these things, all ye nations: * give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.

content.latin: 48:3 Quique terrígenæ, et fílii hóminum: * simul in unum dives et pauper.
content.english: 48:3 All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: * both rich and poor together.

content.latin: 48:4 Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam: * et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
content.english: 48:4 My mouth shall speak wisdom: * and the meditation of my heart understanding

content.latin: 48:5 Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam: * apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
content.english: 48:5 I will incline my ear to a parable; * I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

content.latin: 48:6 Cur timébo in die mala? * iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me:
content.english: 48:6 Why shall I fear in the evil day? * the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.

content.latin: 48:7 Qui confídunt in virtúte sua: * et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
content.english: 48:7 They that trust in their own strength, * and glory in the multitude of their riches,

content.latin: 48:8 Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo: * non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
content.english: 48:8 No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: * he shall not give to God his ransom,

content.latin: 48:9 Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ: * et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
content.english: 48:9 Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: * and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.

content.latin: 48:11 Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes: * simul insípiens, et stultus períbunt.
content.english: 48:11 He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: * the senseless and the fool shall perish together:

content.latin: 48:11 Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas: * et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
content.english: 48:11 And they shall leave their riches to strangers: * and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.

content.latin: 48:12 Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie: * vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
content.english: 48:12 Their dwelling places to all generations: * they have called their lands by their names.

content.latin: 48:13 Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
content.english: 48:13 And man when he was in honour did not understand; * he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Ant. Ne timúeris * cum dívite non descéndet in sepúlcrum glória eius.
content.english: Ant. Be not thou afraid * the things which made him rich, or his glory shall not descend with him to the sepulchre.

content.latin: 48:14 Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis: * et póstea in ore suo complacébunt.
content.english: 48:14 This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them: * and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.

content.latin: 48:15 Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt: * mors depáscet eos.
content.english: 48:15 They are laid in hell like sheep: * death shall feed upon them.

content.latin: 48:15 Et dominabúntur eórum iusti in matutíno: * et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
content.english: 48:15 And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; * and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.

content.latin: 48:16 Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi: * cum accéperit me.
content.english: 48:16 But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, * when he shall receive me.

content.latin: 48:17 Ne timúeris, cum dives factus fúerit homo: * et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus eius.
content.english: 48:17 Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, * and when the glory of his house shall be increased.

content.latin: 48:18 Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia: * neque descéndet cum eo glória eius.
content.english: 48:18 For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; * nor shall his glory descend with him.

content.latin: 48:19 Quia ánima eius in vita ipsíus benedicétur: * confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
content.english: 48:19 For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: * and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.

content.latin: 48:20 Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum: * et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
content.english: 48:20 He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: * and he shall never see light.

content.latin: 48:21 Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intelléxit: * comparátus est iuméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
content.english: 48:21 Man when he was in honour did not understand: * he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.

content.latin: 49:1 Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est: * ‡ et vocávit terram,
content.english: 49:1 The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: * ‡ and he hath called the earth.

content.latin: 49:1 A solis ortu usque ad occásum: * ex Sion spécies decóris eius.
content.english: 49:1 From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof: * out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.

content.latin: 49:3 Deus maniféste véniet: * Deus noster et non silébit.
content.english: 49:3 God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, * and shall not keep silence.

content.latin: 49:3 Ignis in conspéctu eius exardéscet: * et in circúitu eius tempéstas válida.
content.english: 49:3 A fire shall burn before him: * and a mighty tempest shall be round about

content.latin: 49:4 Advocábit cælum desúrsum: * et terram discérnere pópulum suum.
content.english: 49:4 He shall call heaven from above, * and the earth, to judge his people.

content.latin: 49:5 Congregáte illi sanctos eius: * qui órdinant testaméntum eius super sacrifícia.
content.english: 49:5 Gather ye together his saints to him: * who set his covenant before sacrifices.

content.latin: 49:6 Et annuntiábunt cæli iustítiam eius: * quóniam Deus iudex est.
content.english: 49:6 And the heavens shall declare his justice: * for God is judge.

content.latin: 49:7 Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar: Israël, et testificábor tibi: * Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
content.english: 49:7 Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: * I am God, thy God.

content.latin: 49:8 Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te: * holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
content.english: 49:8 I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: * and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.

content.latin: 49:9 Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos: * neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
content.english: 49:9 I will not take calves out of thy house: * nor he goats out of thy flocks.

content.latin: 49:10 Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum: * iuménta in móntibus et boves.
content.english: 49:10 For all the beasts of the woods are mine: * the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.

content.latin: 49:11 Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli: * et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
content.english: 49:11 I know all the fowls of the air: * and with me is the beauty of the field.

content.latin: 49:12 Si esuríero, non dicam tibi: * meus est enim orbis terræ, et plenitúdo eius.
content.english: 49:12 If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: * for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.

content.latin: 49:13 Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum? * aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
content.english: 49:13 Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? * or shall I drink the blood of goats?

content.latin: 49:14 Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis: * et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
content.english: 49:14 Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: * and pay thy vows to the most High.

content.latin: 49:15 Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis: * éruam te, et honorificábis me.
content.english: 49:15 And call upon me in the day of trouble: * I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.

content.latin: 49:16 Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: * Quare tu enárras iustítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
content.english: 49:16 But to the sinner God hath said: * Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?

content.latin: 49:17 Tu vero odísti disciplínam: * et proiecísti sermónes meos retrórsum:
content.english: 49:17 Seeing thou hast hated discipline: * and hast cast my words behind thee.

content.latin: 49:18 Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo: * et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
content.english: 49:18 If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: * and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.

content.latin: 49:19 Os tuum abundávit malítia: * et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
content.english: 49:19 Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, * and thy tongue framed deceits.

content.latin: 49:20 Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum: * hæc fecísti, et tácui.
content.english: 49:20 Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son: * these things hast thou done, and I was silent.

content.latin: 49:21 Existimásti, iníque, quod ero tui símilis: * árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
content.english: 49:21 Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: * but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.

content.latin: 49:22 Intellégite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum: * nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
content.english: 49:22 Understand these things, you that forget God; * lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.

content.latin: 49:23 Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me: * et illic iter, quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
content.english: 49:23 The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: * and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.

content.latin: 50:3 Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 50:3 Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.

content.latin: 50:3 Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
content.english: 50:3 And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.

content.latin: 50:4 Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
content.english: 50:4 Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.

content.latin: 50:5 Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
content.english: 50:5 For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.

content.latin: 50:6 Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.
content.english: 50:6 To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.

content.latin: 50:7 Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
content.english: 50:7 For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.

content.latin: 50:8 Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
content.english: 50:8 For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.

content.latin: 50:9 Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
content.english: 50:9 Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

content.latin: 50:10 Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
content.english: 50:10 To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

content.latin: 50:11 Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
content.english: 50:11 Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.

content.latin: 50:12 Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
content.english: 50:12 Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

content.latin: 50:13 Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
content.english: 50:13 Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.

content.latin: 50:14 Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
content.english: 50:14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

content.latin: 50:15 Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
content.english: 50:15 I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.

content.latin: 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.
content.english: 50:16 Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

content.latin: 50:17 Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: 50:17 O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.

content.latin: 50:18 Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
content.english: 50:18 For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.

content.latin: 50:19 Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
content.english: 50:19 A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

content.latin: 50:20 Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.
content.english: 50:20 Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

content.latin: 50:21 Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
content.english: 50:21 Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.

content.latin: 19 Percússit autem de viris Bethsamítibus, eo quod vidíssent arcam Dómini; et percússit de pópulo septuagínta viros et quinquagínta míllia plebis. Luxítque pópulus, eo quod Dóminus percussísset plebem plaga magna.

content.latin: 1 Venérunt ergo viri Cariathíarim, et reduxérunt arcam Dómini, et intulérunt eam in domum Abínadab in Gábaa: Eleázarum autem fílium eius sanctificavérunt, ut custodíret arcam Dómini.
content.english: 1 So they came as they were bidden, the men of Cariathiarim, and brought back the ark with them, housing it with a certain Abinadab in Gabaa; and they set apart his son Eleazar to keep watch over the Lord's ark.

content.english: 2 And it came to pass, that from the day the ark of the Lord abode in Cariathiarim days were multiplied, (for it was now the twentieth year,) and all the house of Israel rested following the Lord.

content.latin: 3 Ait autem Sámuel ad univérsam domum Israël dicens: Si in toto corde vestro revertímini ad Dóminum, auférte deos aliénos de médio vestri Báalim et Astaroth et præparáte corda vestra Dómino et servíte ei soli, et éruet vos de manu Philísthiim.
content.english: 3 And Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying: If you turn to the Lord with all your heart, put away the strange gods from among you, Baalim and Astaroth: and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.

content.latin: 4 Abstulérunt ergo fílii Israël Báalim et Astaroth, et serviérunt Dómino soli.

content.latin: 5 Dixit autem Sámuel: Congregáte univérsum Israël in Masphath, ut orem pro vobis Dóminum.
content.english: 5 And Samuel said: Gather all Israel to Masphath, that I may pray to the Lord for you.

content.latin: 6 Et convenérunt in Masphath hauserúntque aquam et effudérunt in conspéctu Dómini et ieiunavérunt in die illa atque dixérunt ibi: Peccávimus Dómino. Iudicavítque Sámuel fílios Israël in Masphath.
content.english: 6 And they gathered together to Masphath: and they drew water, and poured it out before the Lord, and they fasted on that day, and they said there: We have sinned against the Lord. And Samuel judged the children of Israel in Masphath.

content.latin: 7 Et audiérunt Philísthiim quod congregáti essent fílii Israël in Masphath, et ascendérunt sátrapæ Philisthinórum ad Israël. Quod cum audíssent fílii Israël, timuérunt a fácie Philisthinórum.
content.english: 7 And the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together to Masphath, and the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the children of Israel heard this, they were afraid of the Philistines.

content.latin: 8 Dixerúntque ad Samuélem: Ne cesses pro nobis clamáre ad Dóminum Deum nostrum, ut salvet nos de manu Philisthinórum.

content.latin: Margaríta, ex régia Anglórum stirpe in Hungária nata, post exáctam summa cum pietáte puerítiam, una cum genitóre, qui a sancto Eduárdo pátruo, Anglórum rege, ad patérni regni fastígium vocabátur, in Angliam, dein in Scótiam venit. Ibi, cum ex matris império Scotórum regi Malchólmo tértio nupsísset, sanctimóniæ et pietátis opéribus annis trigínta toti regno prófuit. Máxima erat in ea vitæ austéritas et flagrantíssimum erga próximos caritátis stúdium, præsértim in egénos; pro quibus aléndis non semel exháusit ærárium. Demum acerbis dolóribus et diutúrno morbo patientíssime tolerátis, ánimam Deo réddidit sextodécimo caléndas decémbris. Quo témporis moménto fácies eius, mácie ac pallóre fœdáta, insólita quadam venustáte reflóruit. Cleméntis décimi auctoritáte in Scótiæ patrónam accépta, ubíque terrárum religiosíssime cólitur.
content.english: Margaret, of the royal house of England, was born in Hungary and spent her childhood there as an unusually devout and pious girl. When her father was called to high office in his own country by his uncle, St. Edward, King of England, she went to England and then to Scotland. There, upon instructions from her mother, she married King Malcolm III. The country was blessed by her holy life and by her deeds of charity for the next thirty years. The austerity of her life was exceedingly great, and her charity towards her neighbour most ardent and zealous, especially for those in need, for whom she not infrequently exhausted the treasury. At length, having most patiently endured bitter sorrows and long illness, she rendered her soul to God on the 16th day of November. At the moment of her death her features, emaciated and pale, bloomed again with unusual beauty. On the authority of Clement X she was chosen Patroness of Scotland, and is honoured with great devotion throughout the world.

content.latin: Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
content.english: All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.

content.latin: Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
content.english: To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.

content.latin: Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
content.english: To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
content.english: bow head Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;

content.latin: Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.

content.latin: Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
content.english: The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
content.english: The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
content.english: The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.

content.latin: Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
content.english: The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;

content.latin: Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
content.english: The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.

content.latin: Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
content.english: Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;

content.latin: Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
content.english: Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.

content.latin: Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
content.english: Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.

content.latin: Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
content.english: Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
content.english: During the following verse all make a profound bow: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.

content.latin: Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
content.english: When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

content.latin: Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
content.english: Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.

content.latin: Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
content.english: We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.

content.latin: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui beátam Margarítam regínam exímia in páuperes caritáte mirábilem effecísti: da; ut, eius intercessióne et exémplo, tua in córdibus nostris cáritas iúgiter augeátur.
content.english: O God, Who didst make Margaret, that blessed Queen, wonderful for tender love toward the poor, grant that her intercession and example may be effectual to gain for our hearts a thorough love toward thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: Psalm 96 [1]

content.latin: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * ‡ læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
content.english: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * ‡ let many islands be glad.

content.latin: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu eius: * iustítia, et iudícium corréctio sedis eius.
content.english: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

content.latin: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos eius.
content.english: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

content.latin: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura eius orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
content.english: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

content.latin: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
content.english: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

content.latin: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli iustítiam eius: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam eius.
content.english: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

content.latin: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
content.english: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

content.latin: 96:7 Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
content.english: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

content.latin: 96:8 Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Iudæ, * propter iudícia tua, Dómine:
content.english: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

content.latin: 96:9 Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.
content.english: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

content.latin: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
content.english: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

content.latin: 96:11 Lux orta est iusto, * et rectis corde lætítia.
content.english: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

content.latin: 96:12 Lætámini, iusti, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis eius.
content.english: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

content.latin: 64:2 Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion: * ‡ et tibi reddétur votum in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 64:2 A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion: * ‡ and a vow shall be paid to thee in Jerusalem.

content.latin: 64:3 Exáudi oratiónem meam: * ad te omnis caro véniet.
content.english: 64:3 O hear my prayer: * all flesh shall come to thee.

content.latin: 64:4 Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos: * et impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis.
content.english: 64:4 The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: * and thou wilt pardon our transgressions.

content.latin: 64:5 Beátus, quem elegísti, et assumpsísti: * inhabitábit in átriis tuis.
content.english: 64:5 Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee: * he shall dwell in thy courts.

content.latin: 64:5 Replébimur in bonis domus tuæ: * sanctum est templum tuum, mirábile in æquitáte.
content.english: 64:5 We shall be filled with the good things of thy house; holy is thy temple, * wonderful in justice.

content.latin: 64:6 Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster, * spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe.
content.english: 64:6 Hear us, O God our saviour, * who art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.

content.latin: 64:7 Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia: * qui contúrbas profúndum maris sonum flúctuum eius.
content.english: 64:7 Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power: * who troublest the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves.

content.latin: 64:8 Turbabúntur gentes, et timébunt qui hábitant términos a signis tuis: * éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis.
content.english: 64:8 The Gentiles shall be troubled, and they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs: * thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful.

content.latin: 64:10 Visitásti terram, et inebriásti eam: * multiplicásti locupletáre eam.
content.english: 64:10 Thou hast visited the earth, and hast plentifully watered it; * thou hast many ways enriched it.

content.latin: 64:10 Flumen Dei replétum est aquis, parásti cibum illórum: * quóniam ita est præparátio eius.
content.english: 64:10 The river of God is filled with water, thou hast prepared their food; * for so is its preparation.

content.latin: 64:11 Rivos eius inébria, multíplica genímina eius: * in stillicídiis eius lætábitur gérminans.
content.english: 64:11 Fill up plentifully the streams thereof, multiply its fruits; * it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers.

content.latin: 64:12 Benedíces corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ: * et campi tui replebúntur ubertáte.
content.english: 64:12 Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness: * and thy fields shall be filled with plenty.

content.latin: 64:13 Pinguéscent speciósa desérti: * et exsultatióne colles accingéntur.
content.english: 64:13 The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat: * and the hills shall be girded about with joy.

content.latin: 64:14 Indúti sunt aríetes óvium, et valles abundábunt fruménto: * clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent.
content.english: 64:14 The rams of the flock are clothed, and the vales shall abound with corn: * they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn.

content.english: Psalm 100 [3]

content.latin: 100:1 Misericórdiam, et iudícium * cantábo tibi, Dómine:
content.english: 100:1 Mercy and judgment * I will sing to thee, O Lord:

content.latin: 100:2 Psallam, et intéllegam in via immaculáta, * quando vénies ad me.
content.english: 100:2 I will sing, and I will understand in the unspotted way, * when thou shalt come to me.

content.latin: 100:2 Perambulábam in innocéntia cordis mei, * in médio domus meæ.
content.english: 100:2 I walked in the innocence of my heart, * in the midst of my house.

content.latin: 100:3 Non proponébam ante óculos meos rem iniústam: * faciéntes prævaricatiónes odívi.
content.english: 100:3 I did not set before my eyes any unjust thing: * I hated the workers of iniquities.

content.latin: 100:4 Non adhǽsit mihi cor pravum: * declinántem a me malígnum non cognoscébam.
content.english: 100:4 The perverse heart did not cleave to me: * and the malignant, that turned aside from me, I would not know.

content.latin: 100:5 Detrahéntem secréto próximo suo, * hunc persequébar.
content.english: 100:5 The man that in private detracted his neighbour, * him did I persecute.

content.latin: 100:5 Supérbo óculo, et insatiábili corde, * cum hoc non edébam.
content.english: 100:5 With him that had a proud eye, and an unsatiable heart, * I would not eat.

content.latin: 100:6 Óculi mei ad fidéles terræ ut sédeant mecum: * ámbulans in via immaculáta, hic mihi ministrábat.
content.english: 100:6 My eyes were upon the faithful of the earth, to sit with me: * the man that walked in the perfect way, he served me.

content.latin: 100:7 Non habitábit in médio domus meæ qui facit supérbiam: * qui lóquitur iníqua, non diréxit in conspéctu oculórum meórum.
content.english: 100:7 He that worketh pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house: * he that speaketh unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.

content.latin: 100:8 In matutíno interficiébam omnes peccatóres terræ: * ut dispérderem de civitáte Dómini omnes operántes iniquitátem.
content.english: 100:8 In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land: * that I might cut off all the workers of iniquity from the city of the Lord.

content.latin: 16:15 Hymnum cantémus Dómino, * hymnum novum cantémus Deo nostro.
content.english: 16:15 Let us sing a hymn to the Lord, * let us sing a new hymn to our God.

content.latin: 16:16 Adonái, Dómine, magnus es tu, et præclárus in virtúte tua, * et quem superáre nemo potest.
content.english: 16:16 O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, and glorious in thy power, * and no one can overcome thee.

content.latin: 16:17 Tibi sérviat omnis creatúra tua: * quia dixísti, et facta sunt:
content.english: 16:17 Let all thy creatures serve thee: * because thou hast spoken, and they were made:

content.latin: 16:18 Misísti spíritum tuum, et creáta sunt, * et non est qui resístat voci tuæ.
content.english: 16:18 Thou didst send forth thy spirit, and they were created, * and there is no one that can resist thy voice.

content.latin: 16:19 Montes a fundaméntis movebúntur cum aquis: * petræ, sicut cera, liquéscent ante fáciem tuam.
content.english: 16:19 The mountains shall be moved from the foundations with the waters: * the rocks shall melt as wax before thy face.

content.latin: 16:20 Qui autem timent te, * magni erunt apud te per ómnia.
content.english: 16:20 But they that fear thee, * shall be great with thee in all things.

content.latin: 16:21 Væ genti insurgénti super genus meum: Dóminus enim omnípotens vindicábit in eis, * in die iudícii visitábit illos.
content.english: 16:21 Woe be to the nation that riseth up against my people: for the Lord almighty will take revenge on them, * in the day of judgment he will visit them.

content.latin: 16:22 Dabit enim ignem, et vermes in carnes eórum, * ut urántur, et séntiant usque in sempitérnum.
content.english: 16:22 For he will give fire, and worms into their flesh, * that they may burn, and may feel for ever.

content.latin: 145:2 Lauda, ánima mea, Dóminum, laudábo Dóminum in vita mea: * psallam Deo meo quámdiu fúero.
content.english: 145:2 Praise the Lord, O my soul, in my life I will praise the Lord: * I will sing to my God as long as I shall be.

content.latin: 145:2 Nolíte confídere in princípibus: * in fíliis hóminum, in quibus non est salus.
content.english: 145:2 Put not your trust in princes: * in the children of men, in whom there is no salvation.

content.latin: 145:4 Exíbit spíritus eius, et revertétur in terram suam: * in illa die períbunt omnes cogitatiónes eórum.
content.english: 145:4 His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth: * in that day all their thoughts shall perish.

content.latin: 145:5 Beátus, cuius Deus Iacob adiútor eius, spes eius in Dómino, Deo ipsíus: * qui fecit cælum et terram, mare, et ómnia, quæ in eis sunt.
content.english: 145:5 Blessed is he who hath the God of Jacob for his helper, whose hope is in the Lord his God: * who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.

content.latin: 145:7 Qui custódit veritátem in sǽculum, facit iudícium iniúriam patiéntibus: * dat escam esuriéntibus.
content.english: 145:7 Who keepeth truth for ever: who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong: * who giveth food to the hungry.

content.latin: 145:7 Dóminus solvit compedítos: * Dóminus illúminat cæcos.
content.english: 145:7 The Lord looseth them that are fettered: * the Lord enlighteneth the blind.

content.latin: 145:8 Dóminus érigit elísos, * Dóminus díligit iustos.
content.english: 145:8 The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down: * the Lord loveth the just.

content.latin: 145:9 Dóminus custódit ádvenas, pupíllum et víduam suscípiet: * et vias peccatórum dispérdet.
content.english: 145:9 The Lord keepeth the strangers, he will support the fatherless and the widow: * and the ways of sinners he will destroy.

content.latin: 145:10 Regnábit Dóminus in sǽcula, Deus tuus, Sion, * in generatiónem et generatiónem.
content.english: 145:10 The Lord shall reign for ever: thy God, O Sion, * unto generation and generation.

content.latin: Salamínæ, in Cypro, natális sancti Bárnabæ Apóstoli, qui, natióne Cýprius, cum Paulo Géntium Apóstolus a discípulis ordinátus, multas regiónes cum eo peragrávit, iniúnctum sibi opus Evangélicæ prædicatiónis exércens; postrémo, Cyprum proféctus, ibi Apostolátum suum glorióso martýrio decorávit. Eius corpus, témpore Zenónis Imperatóris, ipso Bárnaba revelánte, repértum est, una cum códice Evangélii sancti Matthǽi, eiúsdem Bárnabæ manu descrípto.
content.english: The Octave of the most Sacred Body of Christ.

content.latin: Salmánticæ, in Hispánia, item natális sancti Ioánnis a sancto Facúndo, ex Eremitárum sancti Augustíni Ordine, Confessóris; qui fídei zelo, sanctimónia vitæ ac miráculis cláruit. Ipsíus autem festívitas sequénti die celebrátur.
content.english: The holy Apostle Barnabas. He was a Cypriot by birth, was by the disciples ordained an Apostle to the Gentiles along with Paul, and went through many countries with him doing that work of preaching the Gospel which had been laid upon them. In the end he went home to Cyprus, where he crowned the dignity of the Apostolate with the glory of martyrdom. Through a revelation from himself his body was discovered in the time of the Emperor Zeno, having with it a copy of the Gospel according to Matthew written with his own hand.

content.latin: Aquiléiæ pássio sanctórum Felícis et Fortunáti fratrum, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, equúleo suspénsi, atque, ardéntibus lampádibus circa eórum látera appósitis et mox divína virtúte exstínctis, per ventrem fervénti oleo sunt perfúsi; et ad últimum, cum in Christi confessióne persísterent, gloriósi certáminis cursum, obtruncáti cápite, implevérunt.
content.english: At Aquileia, the holy brethren Felix and Fortunatus, both martyrs. In the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian they were hung upon the rack, and lighted lamps put to their sides, but these were extinguished by the power of God. Boiling oil was poured into their bellies, and at last, forasmuch as they still stood firm in confessing Christ, they were beheaded.

content.latin: Tarvísii sancti Parísii, civis Bononiénsis, Confessóris et Mónachi, ex Ordine Camaldulénsi.
content.english: At Rome is commemorated the translation of the body of holy Gregory of Nazianzus. This sacred body had been brought to Rome from Constantinople and had lain for a long time in the church of the Mother of God at the Campus Martius, when the Supreme Pontiff Gregory XIII, [in the year 1580,] removed it with great pomp to the chapel which he had splendidly decorated in the Basilica of St Peter, and there laid it under the altar with due honour.

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

content.latin: 54:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
content.english: 54:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.

content.latin: 54:3 Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
content.english: 54:3 I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.

content.latin: 54:4 Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
content.english: 54:4 For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.

content.latin: 54:5 Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
content.english: 54:5 My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.

content.latin: 54:6 Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
content.english: 54:6 Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.

content.latin: 54:7 Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
content.english: 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?

content.latin: 54:8 Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
content.english: 54:8 Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.

content.latin: 54:9 Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
content.english: 54:9 I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.

content.latin: 54:10 Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
content.english: 54:10 Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.

content.latin: 54:11 Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros eius iníquitas: * et labor in médio eius, et iniustítia.
content.english: 54:11 Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.

content.latin: 54:12 Et non defécit de platéis eius * usúra, et dolus.
content.english: 54:12 And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.

content.latin: 54:13 Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
content.english: 54:13 For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.

content.latin: 54:13 Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
content.english: 54:13 And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.

content.latin: 54:14 Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
content.english: 54:14 But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.

content.latin: 54:15 Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
content.english: 54:15 Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.

content.latin: 54:16 Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
content.english: 54:16 Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.

content.latin: 54:16 Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
content.english: 54:16 For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.

content.latin: 54:17 Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
content.english: 54:17 But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.

content.latin: 54:18 Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
content.english: 54:18 Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.

content.latin: 54:19 Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
content.english: 54:19 He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.

content.latin: 54:20 Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
content.english: 54:20 God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.

content.latin: 54:20 Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
content.english: 54:20 For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.

content.latin: 54:21 Contaminavérunt testaméntum eius, divísi sunt ab ira vultus eius: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
content.english: 54:21 They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.

content.latin: 54:22 Mollíti sunt sermónes eius super óleum: * et ipsi sunt iácula.
content.english: 54:22 His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.

content.latin: 54:23 Iacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem iusto.
content.english: 54:23 Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.

content.latin: 54:24 Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
content.english: 54:24 But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.

content.latin: 54:24 Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
content.english: 54:24 Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.

content.english: Psalm 55 [1]

content.latin: 55:2 Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
content.english: 55:2 Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.

content.latin: 55:3 Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
content.english: 55:3 My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.

content.latin: 55:4 Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
content.english: 55:4 From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.

content.latin: 55:5 In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
content.english: 55:5 In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

content.latin: 55:6 Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
content.english: 55:6 All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.

content.latin: 55:7 Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
content.english: 55:7 They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.

content.latin: 55:8 Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
content.english: 55:8 As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.

content.latin: 55:9 Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
content.english: 55:9 O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,

content.latin: 55:9 Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
content.english: 55:9 As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.

content.latin: 55:10 In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
content.english: 55:10 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.

content.latin: 55:11 In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
content.english: 55:11 In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.

content.latin: 55:12 In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
content.english: 55:12 In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:

content.latin: 55:13 Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
content.english: 55:13 Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 56 [2]
content.english: Psalm 56 [2]

content.latin: 56:2 Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei: * quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
content.english: 56:2 Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: * for my soul trusteth in thee.

content.latin: 56:2 Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo, * donec tránseat iníquitas.
content.english: 56:2 And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, * until iniquity pass away.

content.latin: 56:3 Clamábo ad Deum altíssimum: * Deum qui benefécit mihi.
content.english: 56:3 I will cry to God the most High; * to God who hath done good to me.

content.latin: 56:4 Misit de cælo, et liberávit me: * dedit in oppróbrium conculcántes me.
content.english: 56:4 He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: * he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me.

content.latin: 56:4 Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam, * et erípuit ánimam meam de médio catulórum leónum: dormívi conturbátus.
content.english: 56:4 God hath sent his mercy and his truth, * and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled.

content.latin: 56:5 Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: * et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
content.english: 56:5 The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, * and their tongue a sharp sword.

content.latin: 56:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, * et in omnem terram glória tua.
content.english: 56:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, * and thy glory above all the earth.

content.latin: 56:7 Láqueum paravérunt pédibus meis: * et incurvavérunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 56:7 They prepared a snare for my feet; * and they bowed down my soul.

content.latin: 56:7 Fodérunt ante fáciem meam fóveam: * et incidérunt in eam.
content.english: 56:7 They dug a pit before my face, * and they are fallen into it.

content.latin: 56:8 Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam.
content.english: 56:8 My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.

content.latin: 56:9 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
content.english: 56:9 Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: * I will arise early.

content.latin: 56:10 Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus:
content.english: 56:10 I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: * I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.

content.latin: 56:11 Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua, * et usque ad nubes véritas tua.
content.english: 56:11 For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: * and thy truth unto the clouds.

content.latin: 56:12 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus: * et super omnem terram glória tua.
content.english: 56:12 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: * and thy glory above all the earth.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Psalmus 57 [3]
content.english: Psalm 57 [3]

content.latin: 57:2 Si vere útique iustítiam loquímini: * recta iudicáte, fílii hóminum.
content.english: 57:2 If in very deed you speak justice: * judge right things, ye sons of men.

content.latin: 57:3 Étenim in corde iniquitátes operámini: * in terra iniustítias manus vestræ concínnant.
content.english: 57:3 For in your heart you work iniquity: * your hands forge injustice in the earth.

content.latin: 57:4 Alienáti sunt peccatóres a vulva, erravérunt ab útero: * locúti sunt falsa.
content.english: 57:4 The wicked are alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the womb: * they have spoken false things.

content.latin: 57:5 Furor illis secúndum similitúdinem serpéntis: * sicut áspidis surdæ, et obturántis aures suas,
content.english: 57:5 Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent: * like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears:

content.latin: 57:6 Quæ non exáudiet vocem incantántium: * et venéfici incantántis sapiénter.
content.english: 57:6 Which will not hear the voice of the charmers; * nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely.

content.latin: 57:7 Deus cónteret dentes eórum in ore ipsórum: * molas leónum confrínget Dóminus.
content.english: 57:7 God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth: * the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions.

content.latin: 57:8 Ad níhilum devénient tamquam aqua decúrrens: * inténdit arcum suum donec infirméntur.
content.english: 57:8 They shall come to nothing, like water running down; * he hath bent his bow till they be weakened.

content.latin: 57:9 Sicut cera, quæ fluit, auferéntur: * supercécidit ignis, et non vidérunt solem.
content.english: 57:9 Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away: * fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun.

content.latin: 57:10 Priúsquam intellégerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum: * sicut vivéntes, sic in ira absórbet eos.
content.english: 57:10 Before your thorns could know the brier; he swalloweth them up, * as alive, in his wrath.

content.latin: 57:11 Lætábitur iustus cum víderit vindíctam: * manus suas lavábit in sánguine peccatóris.
content.english: 57:11 The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge: * he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.

content.latin: 57:12 Et dicet homo: Si útique est fructus iusto: * útique est Deus iúdicans eos in terra.
content.english: 57:12 And man shall say: If indeed there be fruit to the just: * there is indeed a God that judgeth them on the earth.

content.english: She hath opened her hand to the needy, and stretched out her hands to the poor. She shall not fear for her house in the cold of snow.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℟. God shall help her * with His countenance.

content.english: ℣. God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved.

content.english: ℟. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui beátam Margarítam regínam exímia in páuperes caritáte mirábilem effecísti: da; ut, eius intercessióne et exémplo, tua in córdibus nostris cáritas iúgiter augeátur.
content.english: O God, Who didst make Margaret, that blessed Queen, wonderful for tender love toward the poor, grant that her intercession and example may be effectual to gain for our hearts a thorough love toward thee.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rerum, Deus, tenax vigor,
content.english: O strength and stay upholding all creation,

content.latin: Immótus in te pérmanens,
content.english: Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,

content.latin: Lucis diúrnæ témpora
content.english: Yet day by day the light in due gradation

content.latin: Succéssibus detérminans:
content.english: From hour to hour through all its changes guide:

content.latin: Largíre lumen véspere,
content.english: Grant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,

content.latin: Quo vita nusquam décidat,
content.english: An eve untouched by shadows of decay,

content.latin: Sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
content.english: The brightness of a holy death-bed blending

content.latin: Perénnis instet glória.
content.english: With dawning glories of th’ eternal day.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Hear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Now and to endless ages art adored.

content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus meus * misericórdia tua prævéniet me.
content.english: Ant. My God, * his mercy shall prevent me.

content.latin: 58:2 Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus: * et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
content.english: 58:2 Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; * and defend me from them that rise up against me.

content.latin: 58:3 Éripe me de operántibus iniquitátem: * et de viris sánguinum salva me.
content.english: 58:3 Deliver me from them that work iniquity, * and save me from bloody men.

content.latin: 58:4 Quia ecce cepérunt ánimam meam: * irruérunt in me fortes.
content.english: 58:4 For behold they have caught my soul: * the mighty have rushed in upon me:

content.latin: 58:5 Neque iníquitas mea, neque peccátum meum, Dómine: * sine iniquitáte cucúrri, et diréxi.
content.english: 58:5 Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord: * without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps.

content.latin: 58:6 Exsúrge in occúrsum meum, et vide: * et tu, Dómine, Deus virtútum, Deus Israël,
content.english: 58:6 Rise up thou to meet me, and behold: * even thou, O Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel.

content.latin: 58:6 Inténde ad visitándas omnes gentes: * non misereáris ómnibus, qui operántur iniquitátem.
content.english: 58:6 Attend to visit all the nations: * have no mercy on all them that work iniquity.

content.latin: 58:7 Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
content.english: 58:7 They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.

content.latin: 58:8 Ecce, loquéntur in ore suo, et gládius in lábiis eórum: * quóniam quis audívit?
content.english: 58:8 Behold they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips: * for who, say they, hath heard us?

content.latin: 58:9 Et tu, Dómine, deridébis eos: * ad níhilum dedúces omnes gentes.
content.english: 58:9 But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them: * thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing.

content.latin: 58:10 Fortitúdinem meam ad te custódiam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia eius prævéniet me.
content.english: 58:10 I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector: * my God, his mercy shall prevent me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 58:12 Deus osténdet mihi super inimícos meos, ne occídas eos: * nequándo obliviscántur pópuli mei.
content.english: 58:12 God shall let me see over my enemies: slay them not, * lest at any time my people forget.

content.latin: 58:12 Dispérge illos in virtúte tua: * et depóne eos, protéctor meus, Dómine:
content.english: 58:12 And scatter them by thy power; * and bring them down, O Lord, my protector:

content.latin: 58:13 Delíctum oris eórum, sermónem labiórum ipsórum: * et comprehendántur in supérbia sua.
content.english: 58:13 For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips: * and let them be taken in their pride.

content.latin: 58:13 Et de exsecratióne et mendácio annuntiabúntur in consummatióne: * in ira consummatiónis, et non erunt.
content.english: 58:13 And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of, when they are consumed: * when they are consumed by thy wrath, and they shall be no more.

content.latin: 58:14 Et scient quia Deus dominábitur Iacob: * et fínium terræ.
content.english: 58:14 And they shall know that God will rule Jacob, * and all the ends of the earth.

content.latin: 58:15 Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
content.english: 58:15 They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.

content.latin: 58:16 Ipsi dispergéntur ad manducándum: * si vero non fúerint saturáti, et murmurábunt.
content.english: 58:16 They shall be scattered abroad to eat, * and shall murmur if they be not filled.

content.latin: 58:17 Ego autem cantábo fortitúdinem tuam: * et exsultábo mane misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 58:17 But I will sing thy strength: * and will extol thy mercy in the morning.

content.latin: 58:17 Quia factus es suscéptor meus, * et refúgium meum, in die tribulatiónis meæ.
content.english: 58:17 For thou art become my support, * and my refuge, in the day of my trouble.

content.latin: 58:18 Adiútor meus, tibi psallam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia mea.
content.english: 58:18 Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing, for thou art God my defence: * my God my mercy.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Psalmus 59 [3]
content.english: Psalm 59 [3]

content.latin: 59:3 Deus, repulísti nos, et destruxísti nos: * irátus es, et misértus es nobis.
content.english: 59:3 God, thou hast cast us off, and hast destroyed us; * thou hast been angry, and hast had mercy on us.

content.latin: 59:4 Commovísti terram, et conturbásti eam: * sana contritiónes eius, quia commóta est.
content.english: 59:4 Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it: * heal thou the breaches thereof, for it has been moved.

content.latin: 59:5 Ostendísti pópulo tuo dura: * potásti nos vino compunctiónis.
content.english: 59:5 Thou hast shewn thy people hard things; * thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow.

content.latin: 59:6 Dedísti metuéntibus te significatiónem: * ut fúgiant a fácie arcus:
content.english: 59:6 Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee: * that they may flee from before the bow:

content.latin: 59:7 Ut liberéntur dilécti tui: * salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me.
content.english: 59:7 That thy beloved may be delivered. * Save me with thy right hand, and hear me.

content.latin: 59:8 Deus locútus est in sancto suo: * lætábor, et partíbor Síchimam: et convállem tabernaculórum metíbor.
content.english: 59:8 God hath spoken in his holy place: * I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem; and will mete out the vale of tabernacles.

content.latin: 59:9 Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim fortitúdo cápitis mei.
content.english: 59:9 Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim is the strength of my head.

content.latin: 59:9 Iuda rex meus: * Moab olla spei meæ.
content.english: 59:9 Juda is my king: * Moab is the pot of my hope.

content.latin: 59:10 In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ súbditi sunt.
content.english: 59:10 Into Edom will I stretch out my shoe: * to me the foreigners are made subject.

content.latin: 59:11 Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
content.english: 59:11 Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?

content.latin: 59:12 Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos? * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
content.english: 59:12 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies?

content.latin: 59:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
content.english: 59:13 Give us help from trouble: * for vain is the salvation of man.

content.latin: 59:14 In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet tribulántes nos.
content.english: 59:14 Through God we shall do mightily: * and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.

content.latin: 127:1 Beáti, omnes, qui timent Dóminum, * ‡ qui ámbulant in viis eius.
content.english: 127:1 Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: * ‡ that walk in his ways.

content.latin: 127:2 Labóres mánuum tuárum quia manducábis: * beátus es, et bene tibi erit.
content.english: 127:2 For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: * blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee.

content.latin: 127:3 Uxor tua sicut vitis abúndans, * in latéribus domus tuæ.

content.latin: 127:3 Fílii tui sicut novéllæ olivárum, * in circúitu mensæ tuæ.
content.english: 127:3 Thy children as olive plants, * round about thy table.

content.latin: 127:4 Ecce, sic benedicétur homo, * qui timet Dóminum.
content.english: 127:4 Behold, thus shall the man be blessed * that feareth the Lord.

content.latin: 127:5 Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion: * et vídeas bona Ierúsalem ómnibus diébus vitæ tuæ.
content.english: 127:5 May the Lord bless thee out of Sion: * and mayst thou see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.

content.latin: 127:6 Et vídeas fílios filiórum tuórum, * pacem super Israël.
content.english: 127:6 And mayst thou see thy children’s children, * peace upon Israel.

content.english: 128:2 Often have they fought against me from my youth: * but they could not prevail over me.

content.latin: 128:3 Supra dorsum meum fabricavérunt peccatóres: * prolongavérunt iniquitátem suam.
content.english: 128:3 The wicked have wrought upon my back: * they have lengthened their iniquity.

content.latin: 128:4 Dóminus iustus concídit cervíces peccatórum: * confundántur et convertántur retrórsum omnes, qui odérunt Sion.
content.english: 128:4 The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners: * let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Sion.

content.latin: 128:6 Fiant sicut fænum tectórum: * quod priúsquam evellátur, exáruit:
content.english: 128:6 Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: * which withereth before it be plucked up:

content.latin: 128:7 De quo non implévit manum suam qui metit, * et sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit.
content.english: 128:7 Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand: * nor he that gathereth sheaves his bosom.

content.latin: 128:8 Et non dixérunt qui præteríbant: Benedíctio Dómini super vos: * benedíximus vobis in nómine Dómini.
content.english: 128:8 And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you: * we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 129:1 De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * ‡ Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
content.english: 129:1 Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: * ‡ Lord, hear my voice.

content.latin: 129:2 Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 129:2 Let thy ears be attentive * to the voice of my supplication.

content.latin: 129:3 Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
